mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10Y-2Y < 0) within the next 6 months, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in the unemployment rate below 4% signals a tight labor market that will drive wage inflation, leading to a hawkish Fed response and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Core PCE inflation remains below 2% over the next 6 months, indicating that wage pressures are not spilling over into broad inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, as measured by the year-over-year change in the Industrial Production Index, signals a supply shock that will drive inflation and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The ISM Manufacturing PMI remains above 50 for the next 3 months, indicating that the supply shock is transitory and not disrupting overall industrial activity.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the federal funds rate, exceeding a 1% increase over the past 6 months, signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Fed pauses its rate hiking cycle within the next 3 months, signaling a dovish pivot that will reverse the negative equity market impact.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in housing starts, as measured by the year-over-year change in the Housing Starts series, signals a weakening consumer sector that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The NAHB Housing Market Index remains above 50 for the next 3 months, indicating that homebuilder sentiment remains positive and the drop in housing starts is likely temporary.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in payroll employment, as measured by the month-over-month change in the Nonfarm Payrolls series, signals a strengthening labor market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Initial jobless claims rise by more than 10% over the next 3 months, signaling a looming labor market slowdown that will negate the positive consumer spending signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in retail sales, as measured by the month-over-month change in the Retail Sales series, signals a surge in consumer spending that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index falls by more than 10 points over the next 3 months, signaling a looming consumer confidence shock that will reverse the positive spending signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the Consumer Price Index, as measured by the year-over-year change in the CPI, signals a broadening inflationary pressure that will drive a hawkish Fed response and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Atlanta Fed's Sticky-Price CPI measure remains below 2% over the next 6 months, indicating that the inflationary pressure is likely transitory and not broadly entrenched.
